title: ExecutionProfile
description:
Response body of POST /v1/route (HTTP 200). The planning-time decision, stamped IMMUTABLY into story frontmatter.

INVARIANT 2 (planning-time immutability): the profile chosen for an execution attempt is frozen. A worker may not re-choose its model mid-attempt; re-routing requires a NEW attempt with a new call to /v1/route.

INVARIANT 1 (three independent axes): harness, model_profile and placement_policy are three separate fields on purpose. No consumer may collapse two of them into one, and nothing here names a physical model or an endpoint - resolving a profile onto physical compute is /v1/place's job, and substituting a different model is never legitimate (invariant 3).

VOCABULARY: harness, model_profile and placement_policy are closed enums taken verbatim from ConfigMap ai/agent-router-catalog, catalog document version 1.0.0, schema_version 1. They are not restated from memory. See README 'Vocabulary coupling' for the change protocol that keeps this file and the catalog in step.

harness.description: Which autonomous coding harness runs the work.

model_profile.description: Logical model/capability profile. The only model-ish name BMAD stamps; the physical model behind it moves by catalog PR underneath a stable profile name.

effort.description: Reasoning-effort tier for the harness session.

cost_class.description:
How THIS ATTEMPT will be paid for. Invariant 4 is written per-attempt ("Billable use is explicit, per-attempt, and recorded"), so this is a property of the attempt, not a copy of the catalog field.

`free` - local GPU, or a free vendor tier.
`subscription` - a seat the operator already pays for (invariant 10: a subscription is NOT an API key, and nothing here authorises centralising an OAuth token or introducing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).
`metered` - billable per-token spend. DEFAULT-DENY (invariant 4).

It normally equals the selected profile's catalog cost_class, and differs exactly when the profile's usual payment path is unavailable and a billable one exists for the same profile - a subscription pool exhausted for the window, say. That case is the reason the distinction matters: it is where an unguarded router would quietly start spending money.

placement_policy.description: Which placement policy /v1/place must resolve this attempt under. Stamped at planning time so that dispatch-time placement cannot silently widen the set of compute the attempt may land on.

fallbacks.description:
Ordered alternatives, most preferred first, for use when the primary choice cannot start AT ALL (e.g. the harness pool is exhausted). Empty array is legal and means 'no fallback: fail the attempt instead'.

A fallback is a NEW ATTEMPT, not a mid-attempt swap (invariant 2). Every entry obeys the same rules as the primary: no metered entry may appear unless the request set allow_metered: true, and the harness enum is equally closed.

metered.description: True only when this attempt is authorized to spend billable API budget. INVARIANT 4 - metered API is default-deny: absence of subscription or local capacity never silently promotes to billable API. True here requires allow_metered: true on the /v1/route request; the router refuses otherwise (see metered_denied).

rationale.description: One human-readable paragraph citing the deciding signals (blast radius, ambiguity, tags, capacity, cost). This is read by a human reviewing a stamped story months later; 'policy said so' is not a rationale.

catalog_document_version.description: Additive, optional. The catalog's own semver `version` field (e.g. "1.0.0"), carried so a stale-catalog message can name a human-meaningful version rather than only a digest. Never a substitute for catalog_version in an equality check.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339. After this instant the decision is stale and MUST be recomputed by calling /v1/route again rather than dispatched. Expiry exists because the inputs (pool temperature, capacity, catalog) move; it is not a cache TTL for the response body.

allOf.description: INVARIANT 4, mechanically: `metered` is true exactly when the selected cost_class is metered. A profile that claims cost_class=metered with metered=false would spend money without authorization; the reverse would record an authorization that bought nothing.

The metered_denied note is only meaningful on a substituted, non-metered result: it says 'the best option was withheld and this is the best remaining one'. It can never accompany a profile that is itself metered.

harness.description:
INVARIANT 16 - the harness axis accepts claude|codex|devin ONLY. `local-agent` exists in the catalog as a RESERVED, supported:false / selectable:false placeholder so the axis is future-proof, and the catalog states router_behaviour: refuse-to-emit. A router that emits it is wrong and must refuse loudly rather than degrade.

llama.cpp, vLLM and llama-swap are INFERENCE RUNTIME, not autonomous coding harnesses, and no harness may be adopted merely to fill an architectural slot. Making `local-agent` selectable requires its own story evaluating a specific harness; no story in EPIC-035 does that.

The redundant `not` clause is deliberate belt-and-braces: it keeps the refusal true even if somebody later widens the enum without reading this description.
harness.$comment: Vocabulary source: catalog v1.0.0 harnesses table, entries with selectable: true.

model_profile.description:
Profile names read verbatim from catalog v1.0.0 (all seven are selectable: true).

INVARIANT 12 - `local-unrestricted` is an ALIGNMENT property, not a quality tier: it is a weaker model than local-code-standard in every respect except refusal behaviour. Its catalog forbidden_for list (security, iam, secrets, prod-iac, destructive-tools) is a HARD EXCLUSION, not a score or a tie-break: a /v1/route request carrying any of those tags must never be auto-selected onto it, however well it otherwise fits. An operator may still choose it explicitly and own that choice.
model_profile.$comment: Vocabulary source: catalog v1.0.0 profiles table.

placement_policy.description: Policy names read verbatim from catalog v1.0.0 policies.placement_policy. `prefer-warm-local` is the catalog default applied when a caller names none. `edge-only` has resolves_today: false - every placement it names is status: planned - so /v1/place answers it with an explicit unavailable result rather than falling through to the cluster.
placement_policy.$comment: Vocabulary source: catalog v1.0.0 policies.placement_policy table.

catalog_version.description:
Content digest of the catalog this decision was computed against: sha256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the rendered catalog document (ConfigMap ai/agent-router-catalog, key catalog.yaml) exactly as mounted, before any parsing. Computed by the router at load time; never written by hand and never equal to the catalog's semver `version` field.

A caller may echo this value back on a later request to assert it is still planning against the same catalog; a mismatch is answered with 409 catalog_version_stale rather than silently served.

fallback.description: One alternative attempt. Exactly three keys: the axes a fallback may change. It deliberately cannot carry an effort tier or a placement policy - those stay as stamped, so a fallback cannot quietly widen the attempt's blast radius.

code.description: Same machine-readable code as the 409 error of the same name. One condition, two carriers: this in-band note when a non-metered substitute exists, and a 409 error envelope when none does. A caller distinguishes them by whether it received a profile at all.

message.description: Human-readable explanation naming what was withheld and why.

obligation.description: The caller's obligation. Proceeding with the returned non-metered profile is legitimate and is the expected path. The alternative is a NEW /v1/route call carrying allow_metered: true, which is a per-attempt human authorization decision - never an automatic retry. A client that retries with allow_metered: true on its own has defeated invariant 4.

withheld.description: The metered option the router would have returned had the request carried allow_metered: true. Recorded so the human authorizing the spend can see exactly what they are authorizing.

metered_denied.description: INVARIANT 4 refusal note. Present on a 200 response when the best option was metered, the request did not set allow_metered: true, and a non-metered option existed; the profile carried alongside it IS that non-metered option. When no non-metered option exists the router returns 409 metered_denied with no profile instead - it never returns the metered choice with a warning attached.
